summary: This Wikipedia-derived note surveys Myanmar (Burma): its history from the Pyu, Mon and Bamar early civilisations through the Pagan, Taungoo and Konbaung dynasties to British colonial rule, independence in 1948, the 1962 military coup, the 1988 8888 Uprising and the 2011 transition to a nominally civilian government. It also covers administrative divisions, religion, ethnic groups, economy, travel access, tourism, education, and Myanmar's evolving foreign relations with the US, ASEAN, China and Bangladesh.
one_line: Overview of Myanmar (Burma), a Southeast Asian state covering its history, ethnic diversity, politics, economy, religion and foreign relations.
key_facts: The Restored Toungoo kings defeated the Portuguese in 1613 and Siam in 1614.
Hanthawaddy forces sacked Ava in 1752, ending the 266-year-old Toungoo Dynasty.
Myanmar is divided into seven states and seven regions, formerly called divisions.
British Burma began exporting crude oil in 1853, making it one of the earliest petroleum producers in the world.
Myanmar produced 75% of the world's teak under British administration.
In 2011 the military junta was officially dissolved following a 2010 general election, and a nominally civilian government was installed.
In the landmark 2015 election, Aung San Suu Kyi's party won a majority in both houses, ending military rule.
The 1988 unrest led to the 8888 Uprising, after which General Saw Maung staged a coup and formed the State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC).
SLORC changed the country's official English name from the "Socialist Republic of the Union of Burma" to the "Union of Myanmar" in 1989.
In May 2013, Thein Sein became the first Myanmar president to visit the White House in 47 years.
Myanmar became a member of ASEAN in 1997 and chaired the forum and hosted the ASEAN Summit in 2014.
The 2014 census recorded 51 million people, and Myanmar's capital is Naypyidaw while its largest city is Yangon (Rangoon).
The Yangon Stock Exchange officially opened for business on Friday, March 25, 2016.
Myanmar's coastline runs along the Bay of Bengal and the Andaman Sea, and the country covers 676,578 square kilometres.
As of July 2013, about 100 political prisoners remained imprisoned, while conflict between the Burmese Army and local insurgent groups continued.

entities.name: Pagan Kingdom
entities.role: Kingdom established in the 1050s under which Burmese language and Theravada Buddhism spread; fell to Mongol invasions

entities.name: Konbaung dynasty
entities.role: Early 19th century dynasty that ruled modern Myanmar and briefly controlled Manipur and Assam

entities.name: Aung San Suu Kyi
entities.role: Opposition leader released from detention; her National League for Democracy party won a majority in the 2015 election

entities.name: Thein Sein
entities.role: Former military commander and president who visited the White House in May 2013

entities.name: Hillary Clinton

entities.name: Barack Obama

entities.name: Ne Win
